summary.text: Wife of Pelias at Iolcus in Apollodorus and Hyginus — daughter of Bias (`bias-aeolid`) — by whom he begot Acastus and the daughters Pisidice, Pelopia, Hippothoe, and Alcestis.

Homonym guard: not Anaxibia daughter of Cratieus, wife of Nestor (`anaxibia-nestor`); not Anaxibia the Danaid bride of Archelaus (`anaxibia-danaid`). Apollodorus notes that some give Pelias's wife as Phylomache, daughter of Amphion, instead (topic pelias-wife-identity).

story.text: When Pelias dwelt in Thessaly he married Anaxibia, daughter of Bias, and begat a son, Acastus, and daughters, Pisidice, Pelopia, Hippothoe, and Alcestis — the royal brood from which the Iolcan succession and the Pheraean queen Alcestis both descend.

Hyginus names the same queen at the wooing of Alcestis: many suitors sought the daughter of Pelias and Anaxibia, Bias' daughter, until Admetus won her by yoking a lion and a boar to a chariot with Apollo's help.
